nodes.name: Sputtering Deposition
nodes.procedure: PtCu2/CuO coatings were deposited on commercially pure-Ti substrates using the sputtering deposition technique in a dual-cathode sputtering deposition system. For comparison, the individual PtCu alloy coating with a Pt:Cu atomic ratio of 1:2 (hereinafter referred to as PtCu2) and individual CuO coating were also prepared via the same process. Details of the target preparation process and coating deposition parameters are provided in the Methods section.

nodes.characterization_summary: PtCu₂/CuO coating surface shows mixture of grooves and small protrusions; PtCu₂ shows grooves; CuO shows small protrusions.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Scanning electron microscope (SEM) analysis revealed that the surface of the PtCu₂/CuO coating exhibits a morphology characterized by a mixture of grooves and small protrusions. In contrast, the surfaces of the CuO and PtCu₂ coatings are dominated by small protrusions and grooves, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: HAADF-STEM reveals clear contrast between bright phase (Pt/Cu enriched) and dark phase (Cu/O enriched) within the PtCu₂/CuO coating with a clear transition layer to Ti substrate.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The high-angle annular dark-field transmission electron microscope (HAADF-STEM) image reveals a clear contrast between bright and dark phases within the coating.

nodes.characterization_summary: CuO phase shows crystal plane spacings of 2.52 Å and 2.53 Å corresponding to (-111) and (002) planes; PtCu₂ phase shows 2.21 Å and 1.95 Å for (111) and (200) planes.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in the HAADF-STEM image of the oxide phase presented in Figure 2c, the measured spacings of the two crystal planes visible are 2.52 and 2.53Å, which correspond, respectively, to the (-111) and (002) crystal planes of the CuO monoclinic crystal structure.

nodes.characterization_summary: EDS confirms Pt:Cu atomic ratio close to 1:2 and Cu:O close to 1:1; element distribution shows Pt/Cu enrichment in bright phase and Cu/O in dark phase.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The analysis of EDS line-scan data reveals that the atomic ratio of Pt and Cu is close to 1:2, while the atomic ratio of Cu and O is close to 1:1.

nodes.characterization_summary: Strain distribution at PtCu₂(111)//CuO(002) heterojunction interface shows tensile stress in FCC-phase and compressive stress in CuO phase.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Furthermore, the strain distribution image at the heterojunction interface based on the geometric phase analysis (GPA) method presents obvious strain fluctuations.

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD confirms coexistence of CuO monoclinic and FCC PtCu₂ metal phases; diffraction peaks for PtCu₂ between elemental Pt and Cu positions due to lattice contraction.
nodes.evidence_snippet: X-ray diffraction (XRD) patterns also confirm the coexistence of the CuO and FCC metal phases in the PtCu₂/CuO coating.

nodes.characterization_summary: PtCu₂/CuO shows Pt²⁺ 32.3% (vs 12.4% in PtCu₂) and Cu²⁺ 57.1% (vs 16.0% in PtCu₂); positive shift in Pt⁰ binding energy indicates electrons flow from PtCu₂ to CuO phase.
nodes.evidence_snippet: From the XPS peak area ratio, the proportions of Pt²⁺ and Cu²⁺ increase, respectively, from 12.4% to 32.3% and from 16.0% to 57.1% after heterostructure formation. This interaction also causes a positive shift in the binding energy of the Pt⁰ characteristic peak.

nodes.characterization_summary: Pt L₃-edge XANES shows increased white line intensity and high-energy shift for PtCu₂/CuO vs Pt foil, indicating electron transfer from PtCu₂ to CuO; Cu K-edge shows metallic Cu in PtCu₂ and oxidized Cu in PtCu₂/CuO.
nodes.evidence_snippet: With the introduction of CuO, the WL intensity for PtCu₂/CuO is higher than that for Pt foil, but much lower than that for PtO₂, indicating that electrons will transfer from PtCu₂ to CuO through the heterojunction interface.

nodes.characterization_summary: EXAFS shows Pt-Pt/Cu, Cu-Pt/Cu metallic bonds plus Pt-O, Cu-O oxidized bonds and additional Pt-O-Cu, Cu-O-Cu bonds in PtCu₂/CuO heterojunction.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In the corresponding extended X-ray absorption fine structure (EXAFS) spectra for the Pt L₃-edge and Cu K-edge, PtCu₂/CuO not only exhibits Pt-Pt/Cu and Cu-Pt/Cu bonds belonging to the metallic state, but also Pt-O and Cu-O bonds belonging to the oxidized state.
